steps.text: Coding agents like Claude Code now work for hours on their own.
But they still need me. When I step away from my screen, the agent stops, and waits.
Today, all it can do is send a notification. I see it an hour later, and the work just sat there.
What I need is simple. My agent should be able to call me, and I should be able to call it.
{{product}} gives any text agent a real voice, and a phone number.
It sits between people and their agents. It listens, keeps answers short, asks before it acts, and calls back when there's news.
Here's how it works with my Claude Code, running in the cloud. I'm out for a walk, so I call it.
Hey. Did last night's test run pass?
Mostly. Two hundred twelve of two hundred fourteen tests passed. Two checkout tests failed after yesterday's payment change. Want me to look into it?
Yes. Fix them and open a pull request. But don't merge.
Got it. I'll fix both tests and open a pull request, without merging. It'll take a few minutes. I'll call you back.
I hang up. The agent keeps working in the cloud.
Hi, it's Claude Code. I found it: a rounding bug in the new currency code. Both tests pass now. One question first. Refunds use the same code. Should I fix them too?
Done. All two hundred fourteen tests pass, and the pull request is open. I've texted you the link.
Claude Code did the work. {{product}} did the talking. It kept it short, it asked before deciding, and it called me back.
